title: RedFlag_Trail
tagline: See what AI agents spend on x402 — and block risky payments in the wallet before they're signed.
description:
RedFlag_Trail is built as a live pipeline across three partner integrations.

The Graph: a Substreams package ("papertrail") composes the official x402 module with erc20-tokens, streaming live Base mainnet payments into a Postgres ledger via substreams-sink-sql. Token decimals are sourced by batched eth_call since no prebuilt package carries them. Vendors are enriched against the live ERC-8004/Agent0 subgraph on Base to check registry status.

Privy: wallet policies are default-deny, with an explicit ALLOW scoped to Base (chainId 8453) plus a DENY rule per flagged vendor, keyed on the EIP-3009 `to` field inside eth_signTypedData_v4's typed-data message — never on tx.from or eth_sendTransaction, since the agent never calls the latter. Human approval is a real 2-of-2 Privy key quorum: we implemented the full authorization-signature spec by hand (RFC 8785 canonical JSON → SHA-256 → ECDSA P-256 → DER → base64), since Privy's docs don't give a worked example. Privy itself refuses unsigned and 1-of-2-signed policy changes — the quorum is enforced server-side, not by our app.

Bazantic: we published a Recipe ("agent-spend-audit") on a gateway serving live x402 402-challenges, and ran a controlled A/B test — same model, same tools, the Recipe as the only variable — showing it drives the agent to cite 13 verifiable transaction hashes versus zero, and add honesty guardrails (nothing-enforced disclosure, human-quorum requirement, unpriced≠zero, heuristic confidence) that the raw API spec alone doesn't produce.

A backtest engine (lib/backtest.mjs) replays any proposed rule over indexed history before it can be approved, flagging vendors with many independent payers as false positives. An MCP server exposes 5 tools (spend_summary, vendor_risk, list_findings, backtest_rule, propose_enforcement) so any agent framework can call the same audit. A review console and REST API sit on top for human operators. Everything is reproducible end-to-end with one command: `node scripts/e2e-demo.mjs`.
